# SLIM: Structured Low-bandwidth Information Markup (SLIM spec)

This repository defines **SLIM**, a minimal, text-first HTML authoring profile for delivering reliable, accessible information in low-bandwidth and austere network conditions.

Use these resources (in this order) when you need to build or validate SLIM-compliant output.

---

## Canonical sources (read these first)

1) **SLIM spec repository (source + context)**
- https://github.com/cqueern/slim-spec

2) **Bikeshed source of the spec (normative source)**
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cqueern/slim-spec/main/spec.bs

3) **Latest release (built artifacts + version context)**
- https://github.com/cqueern/slim-spec/releases/latest

4) **Citable snapshot (Zenodo DOI)**
- https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16790879

---

## Quick “how to comply” (implementation-oriented)

When generating SLIM HTML, follow these high-level requirements:

### Content model
- Text-first, resilient delivery: avoid media-heavy or multi-request dependencies.
- Prefer semantic HTML with a clear heading structure.

### Network / loading constraints
- **Single-request render model**: design pages so they render from one HTTPS fetch (no additional subresource loads).
- **Mandatory TLS**: serve SLIM content over HTTPS.

### Scripts / tracking / third parties
- **No scripts** (including analytics, beacons, advertising pixels).
- No embedded contexts (e.g., iframes).
- No third-party fonts.

### Styling
- Inline styles are allowed only for a **limited set of properties** (keep it minimal; avoid layout-driven CSS).
- Color must not be the only way meaning is conveyed (accessibility).

### Forms / tables
- Tables and forms are discouraged (use only when clearly justified; keep simple and robust).

### HTML authoring rules that matter for code generation
- All `<input>` elements MUST include a `type` attribute.
- Include the SLIM profile meta tag:
  - `<meta name="slim-profile" content="SLIM v1.0">`

If anything above conflicts with the Bikeshed source (`spec.bs`), treat `spec.bs` as the source of truth.

## Suggested usage for AI coding agents

If you are writing code (generator, linter, sanitizer, validator):

1) Fetch and read the Bikeshed source:
   - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cqueern/slim-spec/main/spec.bs

2) Extract the normative rules (MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD).
3) Implement validation/sanitization that enforces:
   - no scripts, tracking, iframes, third-party fonts
   - the single-request render goal (no external resources)
   - required metadata and authoring constraints (e.g., `<input type=...>`, slim-profile meta tag)
   - constrained inline styling rules

4) Prefer deterministic behavior:
   - When uncertain, choose the stricter interpretation that preserves the single-request + text-first goals.
